To play Dungeons & Dragons (D&D), follow these steps: 1) The Game Master (GM) describes a scene to set the context for the players. 2) Players describe what their characters do in response to the scene. 3) The GM narrates the results of the adventurers' actions, which may involve challenges requiring decisions or dice rolls. In combat, positions are established first, followed by rolling for Initiative to determine turn order. Combat is organized into rounds where each participant takes a turn based on their Initiative roll until combat concludes. Advantage allows using the higher of two d20 rolls while disadvantage uses the lower one; if both apply, they cancel out, resulting in a single roll. Ability Scores and Modifiers are used for various game mechanics: - Score 12–13 has a modifier of +1 - Score 14–15 has a modifier of +2 - Score 16–17 has a modifier of +3 - Score 18–19 has a modifier of +4 - Score 20 has a modifier of +5. In the Point Cost method, the cost for each ability score is as follows: a score of 8 costs 0 points, 9 costs 1 point, 10 costs 2 points, 11 costs 3 points, 12 costs 4 points, 13 costs 5 points, 14 costs 7 points, and 15 costs 9 points.
